title: Live imaging Arabidopsis thaliana embryos under different hydration conditions
protocol: Prepare solutions of varying levels of water potential.
Prepare a stock solution containing a high concentration of an osmolyte of your choice that will be used to modify the water potential.
Mix 17.532 g NaCl in double-distilled water and adjust volume to 50 mL.
Prepare dilutions of the stock solutions.
Create a 10 mL secondary stock of 2 M NaCl solution.
Prepare 2 mL solutions from 0 M to 2 M in increments of 200 mM.
Submerge 2-3 seeds in 0.5-1 mL of osmolyte solutions prepared.
Invert the Eppendorf tube to ensure that the seeds sink to the bottom.
Incubate for 15-30 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C).
Pipette one seed with approximately 5-10 μL of the solution in which it was submerged.
Place the pipetted seed on a cover slip or slide.
Hold the seed between tweezer tips under a dissecting microscope at 3× magnification.
Hold an Arabidopsis seed between tweezer tips.
Superficially scrape the seed coat and endosperm off with a tungsten needle without damaging the embryo.
Create a cavity by scraping the seed coat and endosperm.
Gently push the embryo through the created cavity to remove the seed coat and endosperm.
Pipette out the seed coat and endosperm debris.
Add 20–50 μL of osmolyte solution or glycerin depending on the condition.
Place a cover slip on top.
Proceed immediately to imaging.
Rinse tweezers and needle with water between each dissection.
Wipe tweezers and needle between each dissection.
Prepare standard growth medium using Murashige and Skoog (MS) recipe.
Adjust pH to 5.7 using potassium hydroxide before adding agar.
Autoclave MS medium using a liquid cycle (20–30 min, 121°C).
Weigh the osmolyte of choice needed to generate a 5–10× stock medium.
For NaCl, weigh 29.22 g to make a 1M stock solution.
Autoclave a bottle containing the weighed osmolyte using a dry cycle (20–30 min, 121°C).
Fill the autoclaved bottle with the media prepared previously to the required volume.
For NaCl preparation, add MS medium to the 29.22 g of NaCl for a final volume of 500 mL to obtain a 1M NaCl solution.
Prepare diluted media at the desired concentrations using the stock medium.
Cool the bottles containing the media to 50°C in a water bath set at 50°C before plating.
Plate the media in a sterile, laminar flow hood.
Gently shake the bottle to mix its content.
Pipette 40 mL into square petri dishes (120 × 120 wide × 15 mm high).
Close the plates as soon as they dry (∼10 min) to avoid evaporation.
Place seeds in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and add 1–1.5 mL of freshly prepared 70% ethanol (70:30 v/v ethanol:double-distilled water).
Vortex for 5 minutes.
Discard the solution and add 1 mL of 100% ethanol.
Pipette seeds onto pre-sterilized filter papers.
Let seeds dry on the filter papers for at least 20 minutes.
Place seeds onto the agar plates by gently tapping them off the filter papers.
Ensure that seeds are spaced out; separate touching seeds with a sterile toothpick.
Seal the plates with micropore surgical tape (3M).
Place the plates in the dark at 4°C for 3–5 days for stratification.
Move the plates to a growth cabinet at 22°C–23°C after stratification.
Maintain conditions of 16 h light/8 h dark and 130 μmol m−2 s−1 PPFD with 50%–60% relative humidity.
Pick 2–3 seeds from the plates using a sterile toothpick or equivalent.
Submerge picked seeds in 0.5–1 mL glycerin.
Work in sterile conditions if the experiment involves a time series.
Place the plate back in its experimental conditions until the next time point.
Dissect seeds as described in step 3.
Proceed immediately to imaging.
Open the Leica Application Suite X software.
Select resonant mode when prompted.
In the “Laser Config” tab, turn on the white light laser and set to 70%.
In the “Hardware” tab, enable “Line Average during Live Acquisition” and set the “Bit Depth Resolution” at 12 bit.
In the “USB Panel” tab, select the “Fine” option for the “Phase” setting.
Enable “Bidirectional X” in the “Acquisition” tab.
Set the “Line Average” to 32 in the “Acquisition” tab.
Set the “Zoom Factor” at 1.25.
Set the excitation wavelength at 488 nm if using GFP.
Select the HC PL APO CS2 63×/1.20 WATER objective if samples are mounted in aqueous solutions.
Select the 63/1.30 GLYCERIN objective if samples are mounted in glycerin.
Turn on one of the HyD SMD detectors and set a detection interval of 50 nm starting at least 10 nm higher than the emission wavelength.
Set the detection interval from 500–550 nm for GFP.
Set the lifetime gate filter at 1.00–6.00 ns.
Turn on PMT Trans under TLD mode.
Load sample using appropriate immersion media for objective used.
Start with wild-type ecotype to familiarize with protein storage vacuoles' autofluorescence.
Find and focus on the sample.
Adjust the gain on the transmitted light channel.
Start with a low laser intensity, e.g., 1% of the laser intensity.
Increase the laser intensity until the HyD SMD channel detects the fluorescence signal without reaching saturation.
Assess saturation by viewing the acquisition through its intensity values using the “Over-/underexposure” button.
Adjust the laser intensity until only a minimal number of pixels appear blue.
Turn off gating while setting up the laser intensity to avoid damaging the detector.
Adjust the phase so that the image appears clear.
Set the Z-Stack.
Adjust the Line Average number if the signal appears grainy.
Start image acquisition.
